payload.prfaq: PRESS RELEASE: quackitect gates now reach the owner's phone - an offer pushes a one-tap bless to a paired ntfy channel and the tap returns a hash-bound, channel-stamped grant within the 6h window, so a decision no longer waits for the owner to reach the desk. HOSTILE FAQ: Q1 'Can a stranger who guesses the topic bless a gate?' - authenticity IS possession of the paired credential; this is the accepted, owner-red-teamed risk (adr-answer-authenticity), mitigated by high-entropy topics, correlation-id matching, idempotent dedup, with a token-ACL upgrade path recorded - answered from the inherited decision, not re-litigated. Q2 'Are you wiring a live internet endpoint that can close my gates while I'm gone?' - NO; the build proves the mechanism against a mock transport only; the live topic is the owner-physical pairing step, never touched unattended (R2). Q3 'Who holds the ntfy secret?' - the owner, in a config file the agent reads but never mints, logs, or enters (R3); a missing config disables the lane and the board still works. Q4 'What if two taps arrive, or a tap for an offer that already expired?' - idempotent: the correlation id must match the LIVE offer hash, and a resolved/absent offer ignores the tap (R4). Q5 'Why not just reply yes over ntfy?' - a bless must be hash-bound and channel-stamped for the audit chain; the X-Actions tap carries the correlation id, a bare reply does not - plain-reply is the documented degraded path only.
payload.findings_folded: One fold: Q3 sharpened R3 and the scope - the credential is explicitly owner-config-only with graceful-disable-on-absent, now a named pass line in one-pager B. Q1/Q2/Q4/Q5 all answered from the inherited decisions and the already-logged risks - no upstream change; the design's maturity (owner-ruled in v1, re-verified 2026-07-21) is why the FAQ finds no new hole.
